# Hildeberto Jardón-Kojakhmetov

> Assistant professor at the Bernoulli Institute for Mathematics, Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence, University of Groningen (the Netherlands). Works in dynamical systems: geometric and singular perturbation methods for multiscale and networked systems, with applications in complex physical and biological systems.

Research themes:

- Slow–fast dynamics and critical transitions: geometric mechanisms behind abrupt transitions, delayed loss of stability and multiscale instabilities (geometric singular perturbation theory, canards, critical transitions, multiscale bifurcations).
- Bifurcation, singularity theory and desingularization: non-hyperbolic points in slow–fast systems as organizing centers of global dynamics, analyzed with blow-up methods (geometric desingularization, non-hyperbolic singularities).
- Networked dynamical systems: how network structure, adaptivity and higher-order (hypergraph) interactions shape collective dynamics and the validity of reduction methods.
- Control of multiscale and networked systems: feedback strategies that stabilize slow–fast systems at non-hyperbolic points, control of canard cycles, and control of networked, polynomial and co-evolutionary systems (stabilization, feedback control, model order reduction, port-Hamiltonian systems).

Contact: h.jardon.kojakhmetov@rug.nl. Students interested in Bachelor, Master or PhD projects in these areas are welcome to get in touch.
